subject: Polity
description: Vice-President: election, qualifications, role as RS Chairman, Article 63-71

questions.stem: The Vice President of India is elected by an electoral college consisting of:

options.option_text: All MPs of both Houses (LS + RS)
All MPs of both Houses + state MLAs

questions.explanation: Article 66 — VP is elected by an ELECTORAL COLLEGE consisting of MEMBERS OF BOTH HOUSES of Parliament (LS + RS, including nominated). MLAs do NOT vote for VP. (Contrast: PRESIDENT — elected by MPs + state MLAs by weighted formula.) Election by SECRET BALLOT, single transferable vote system, proportional representation. Distractor 1 = how the President is elected. Distractor 4 also wrong — that's the President.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Vice President is the EX-OFFICIO chairman of the:
questions.explanation: Article 64 — VP is EX-OFFICIO Chairman of the RAJYA SABHA. Presides over RS sessions. Has CASTING VOTE (like LS Speaker) only in case of tie. VP is NOT a member of either House. Distractor 1: LS is presided over by SPEAKER (elected from amongst LS members). Distractor 4: JOINT SITTING is presided over by LS Speaker (Article 118), not VP.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: MINIMUM AGE qualification for becoming Vice President is:
questions.explanation: Article 66(3) — Qualifications for VP: (a) Indian CITIZEN; (b) at least 35 YEARS of age; (c) qualified to be a member of RAJYA SABHA. Same age as President. NOT an MP at time of election (must give up if elected). NOT hold any office of profit in govt. (Article 66(4)). 5-YEAR term (Article 67); can be re-elected.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The first Vice President of India was:
questions.explanation: Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan — FIRST VP (1952-62), then 2nd PRESIDENT (1962-67). Philosopher, scholar (Eastern Religions + Western Thought; Idealist View of Life); served as Oxford professor + Indian ambassador to USSR; later Chancellor of Delhi University; Bharat Ratna 1954. His birthday — 5 SEPTEMBER — celebrated as TEACHERS' DAY in India. Distractor 1: Rajendra Prasad was first PRESIDENT (1950-62). Distractor 3: V.V. Giri was 4th VP + 4th President. Distractor 4: same person.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: When the office of the President falls vacant, the Vice President:

options.option_text: Continues only as Rajya Sabha Chairman
Acts as President until new one is elected
Election for new President is bypassed
Steps down from VP post immediately

questions.explanation: Article 65 — When PRESIDENT's office is vacant (death, resignation, removal), the VP DISCHARGES the functions of PRESIDENT (acts as President) UNTIL a new President is elected (which must be within 6 MONTHS, Article 62). During this period, VP is no longer the Rajya Sabha Chairman; the DEPUTY CHAIRMAN of RS presides. VV GIRI (3rd VP, 1967-69) became Acting President when Zakir Hussain (3rd President) died in office (1969). Then Giri resigned VP, contested + won presidential election. Mohammad Hidayatullah (CJI) was Acting President for the brief period.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The TERM of the Vice President's office is:

options.option_text: 4 years and ends with general elections
5 years from the date of taking office
6 years like the Rajya Sabha members

questions.explanation: Article 67 — VP holds office for 5 YEARS from date of entering office. Eligible for RE-ELECTION (no term limit, like President). Can be removed earlier by: RESOLUTION of RAJYA SABHA passed by EFFECTIVE majority + agreed by LS by SIMPLE majority. (Note: only RS initiates removal, with 14-day notice.) NO IMPEACHMENT process like President's. RESIGNATION addressed to PRESIDENT.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which Indian Vice President later went on to become PRESIDENT (a common career path)?

options.option_text: No VP has ever become India's President
Only one — Hamid Ansari became President later

questions.explanation: MANY Indian VPs have gone on to become Presidents: S. RADHAKRISHNAN (VP 1952-62 → Pres 1962-67); ZAKIR HUSAIN (VP 1962-67 → Pres 1967-69); V.V. GIRI (VP 1967-69 → Pres 1969-74); R. VENKATARAMAN (VP 1984-87 → Pres 1987-92); SHANKAR DAYAL SHARMA (VP 1987-92 → Pres 1992-97); K.R. NARAYANAN (VP 1992-97 → Pres 1997-2002). Recent exceptions: Krishna Kant (died in office), Bhairon Singh Shekhawat (lost the 2007 presidential election to Pratibha Patil), Hamid Ansari (didn't contest), Venkaiah Naidu, Jagdeep Dhankhar.
